passage: Sahil here, I live by the colony gate. Dolma, five, ran towards the road after her ball. Her mother called, "Dolma, stop!" and Dolma froze mid-step while the ball rolled on. A scooter passed. Her mother walked up and said, "Thank you for stopping." Dolma looked at the ball, then at her mother. I can't tell if she was scared or just startled. In all the weeks I've watched, her mother rarely raises her voice.

qa.q: What might Dolma have felt when she froze?
qa.a: Startled or scared, since she stopped instantly. She might also just have been surprised by the loud call.

qa.q: Why might it help that her mother rarely raises her voice?
qa.a: Warnings kept for real danger keep their power, so Dolma stops when she hears one.

qa.q: How might Dolma's mother feel after the scooter passed?
qa.a: Probably relieved and a bit shaky, hinted by her walking straight up to thank Dolma.

grounding: Shows a child hearing a caution and stopping to look, with an adult who keeps warnings for real danger, seen by a neighbour.

passage: On Monday Kashish said "careful" about a spoon, a crumb and a sock, and Sachin, four, kept running. On Wednesday he raced towards the balcony door and she said, "Sachin, stop." He kept going until she caught him. That night she decided to save her warning words for real danger. On Saturday, when he reached for the hot pan, she said quietly and firmly, "Sachin, stop. Hot." He froze, hand in the air, and looked at her.

qa.q: What did Kashish say when Sachin reached for the hot pan?
What does Sachin's frozen hand suggest he understood on Saturday?
qa.a: That this warning was serious, since her tone was quiet and firm and unlike her usual "careful". He could also just have been startled by her different voice.

qa.q: What did Kashish change, and why did it work?
qa.a: She stopped using warning words for small things and kept them for real danger, so they signal him to stop and look.

qa.q: How might Sachin have experienced all the "careful"s on Monday?
qa.a: As background chatter he had learned to tune out, so none of them stood out as urgent.

grounding: Shows a child who ignores constant cautions but stops for a rare, clear warning about real danger.
